page: Microsoft Azure EC4as_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ECasv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD processor and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include any local storage, meaning it relies entirely on external storage options, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable. There are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with this instance.

With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the EC4as_v6 is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require a larger memory footprint relative to compute capacity. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without resource contention from other tenants. However, the lack of local storage requires users to provision external network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs depending on the storage tier selected. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a high density of memory per vCPU, making it suitable for workloads that are constrained by RAM rather than raw processing power. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and mid-sized enterprise applications.
